prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building accessibility checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Gather the documentation.
3. Ask the right questions.
4. Properly support the documentation.

Part of our building accessibility consulting business is taking sworn engineering statements to court [25 U.S.C. § 6106(3) (b) (2014)]. When a department of justice (DOJ) or state attorney general investigates complaints under Title III or Section 504, they need sworn Expert Witness Reports, statements, testimony or other documents to identify “unreasonable barriers to access.” Deficiencies have to relate to something that you have clear documentation of in order to identify them in a sworn document for the court. If the documentation doesn’t exist, anyone writing a report cannot say that or shouldn’t say that there is a problem. The documentation is the key to making the engineering statement.

AccessBoard Standards (2010 ADA Standards and 2011 UNIFORM Federal Accessibility Standards U
